title: Multimodality detection of early relapse in radically treated high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: study protocol for a prospective multicentre UK cohort study (HERD).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for reliable biomarkers for early relapse in high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), given the high recurrence rate and the current limitations in post-treatment surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective, observational cohort study involving up to 200 patients with stage III/IV HPV-negative HNSCC from secondary and tertiary NHS hospitals in the UK, with a focus on developing and validating a multimodal recurrence risk prediction model.
analysis.methods: The study will integrate imaging, genomic, immunologic, and microbiome datasets using machine learning and Bayesian modelling to develop a recurrence risk prediction model.
analysis.main_results: The study aims to identify patient populations for primary treatment stratification, establish a longitudinal biorepository, and determine biological mechanisms of recurrence, with findings to be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and scientific meetings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study's novel approach involves the integration of multiple data modalities to improve relapse risk prediction and stratification in high-risk HPV-negative HNSCC patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could lead to more effective post-treatment surveillance and stratification of patients, potentially improving survival rates by enabling timely surgical interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the lack of randomization and the potential for confounding factors, but it is designed to provide valuable insights into relapse risk prediction and patient stratification.

analysis.summary_en: This study aims to develop a multimodal recurrence risk prediction model for high-risk HPV-negative HNSCC by integrating imaging, genomic, immunologic, and microbiome datasets, addressing the current limitations in post-treatment surveillance and stratification.

title: Predicting parental Human papillomavirus vaccine hesitancy: development and internal validation of machine learning models

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer is Cameroon’s second most common cancer among women. However, high parental Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine hesitancy impedes elimination, and no validated predictive tool exists.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models predicting parental HPV vaccine hesitancy in the Buea Health District and identify key predictors. Data were split 80/20 into training (n=925) and test (n=231) sets.
analysis.methods: Methods This secondary analysis used cross-sectional survey data from 1,156 parents of children aged 9–18 years. Twenty-six predictor groups were screened via group LASSO (17 retained for logistic regression; all 26 for tree-based models). Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were tuned via repeated cross-validation while thresholds were set by Youden’s J statistic.
analysis.main_results: Results All models showed comparable discrimination (AUC-ROC 0.841–0.870). XGBoost had the highest AUC (0.870, vs 0.869 for logistic regression, DeLong p=0.965); logistic regression had the highest sensitivity (73.1%), F1-score (74.9%), and lowest Brier score (0.1435). Calibration slopes exceeded 1 (1.12–1.46) across models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Hesitancy was more strongly predicted by information access and institutional trust than sociodemographic disadvantage. Insufficient vaccine information, perceived vaccine unsafety, and distrust in the Ministry of Health were the dominant predictors across the models and interpretability analyses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the development and external validation of simple, interpretable prediction tools to identify parents who may benefit from targeted, trust-building vaccine communication and community engagement to support HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The three models achieved comparable, clinically meaningful discrimination, and algorithmic complexity did not improve prediction over standard regression.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models to predict parental HPV vaccine hesitancy in the Buea Health District. The researchers used cross-sectional survey data from 1,156 parents of children aged 9–18 years, screening 26 predictor groups and tuning three models: logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. All models showed comparable discrimination, with XGBoost achieving the highest AUC and logistic regression showing the highest sensitivity and F1-score. The dominant predictors of hesitancy were insufficient vaccine information, perceived vaccine unsafety, and distrust in the Ministry of Health. The authors concluded that trust-building engagement is more effective than broad demographic campaigns in addressing vaccine hesitancy. The findings suggest the potential for developing simple, interpretable prediction tools to support targeted communication and community engagement for HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention. However, the study found that algorithmic complexity did not improve prediction over standard regression, indicating that simpler models may be sufficient. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's design and the absence of external validation.

title: Retrospective Study of Wandai Decoction Plus Recombinant Human Interferon Alpha-2b in Persistent High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the clinical outcomes of using Wandai Decoction (WDT) plus recombinant human interferon α-2b (rhIFN-α-2b) in patients with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection and a spleen-deficiency pattern, focusing on vaginal microecology and peripheral T-cell subsets.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study analyzed clinical data from 125 patients treated between March 2024 and September 2025, with 57 patients receiving WDT plus rhIFN-α-2b vaginal suppositories and 68 patients receiving rhIFN-α-2b alone.
analysis.methods: The study involved evaluating clinical outcomes through analysis of patient data, including HPV conversion rates, vaginal microecological parameters, peripheral T-cell subsets, and symptom improvements, with both groups receiving three consecutive treatment courses.
analysis.main_results: The observation group had a higher total effective rate (89.47% vs. 72.06%, p = 0.015) and a shorter time to first HPV conversion (P = 0.028) compared to the control group, while the overall four-category HPV outcome distribution (P = 0.060) and HPV16/18-specific conversion rate (P = 0.138) did not differ significantly.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that WDT plus rhIFN-α-2b may improve clinical outcomes in patients with persistent high-risk HPV infection, particularly in terms of HPV conversion and vaginal microecology, though the retrospective design limits causal conclusions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform future studies on integrative treatments for persistent high-risk HPV infection and contribute to understanding the role of traditional Chinese medicine in managing HPV-related conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and potential residual confounding limit the strength of the evidence, and the findings should be interpreted cautiously without definitive causal conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study investigated the clinical outcomes of Wandai Decoction (WDT) plus recombinant human interferon α-2b (rhIFN-α-2b) in patients with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection and a spleen-deficiency pattern. The study included 125 patients treated between March 2024 and September 2025, divided into two groups: one receiving WDT plus rhIFN-α-2b vaginal suppositories and the other receiving rhIFN-α-2b alone. Both groups underwent three consecutive treatment courses. The observation group showed a higher total effective rate (89.47% vs. 72.06%, p = 0.015) and a shorter time to first HPV conversion (P = 0.028) compared to the control group. However, the overall four-category HPV outcome distribution (P = 0.060) and HPV16/18-specific conversion rate (P = 0.138) did not differ significantly. More favorable vaginal microecological findings, including lower pH and higher rates of normal hydrogen peroxide status, were observed in the observation group. Post-treatment, CD4+ T-cell percentage and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio were higher, while CD8+ T-cell percentage was lower in the observation group. The study highlights potential benefits of WDT plus rhIFN-α-2b in managing persistent HR-HPV infection but emphasizes the limitations of the retrospective design and the need for further research to establish causality.

title: Global policy determinants of national human papillomavirus vaccine introductions in 2006-2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Although safe and effective human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines have been available since 2006, national introduction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) has progressed slowly. HPV vaccine adoption may have been shaped by evolving World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations, funding policies of Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and the disruption from the Coronavirus Disease 2019 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed policy determinants of national HPV vaccine introduction rate in LMICs from 2006 to 2025.
analysis.methods: This study used generalized linear model (GLM) to assess predetermined policy events and changepoint analysis to identify shifts in adoption trends.
analysis.main_results: Across a range of GLMs exploring different events and outcome variables, WHO's one-dose recommendation in 2022 was most strongly associated with an increase in country introductions, with the expansion of Gavi's funding policy for HPV vaccines (2017-2025) also important in some models. Comparing model projections with and without the one-dose schedule yielded an estimated 22.46 additional national HPV vaccine introductions in LMICs. Changepoint analysis identified a significant increase in introductions in 2022.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results quantify the primary global drivers of HPV vaccine uptake, offering actionable insights for expanding equitable vaccine access.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer actionable insights for expanding equitable vaccine access and inform strategies to accelerate HPV vaccine introduction in LMICs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report limitations, but the evidence is based on model projections and changepoint analysis, which may have inherent uncertainties.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the policy determinants influencing the national introduction of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) from 2006 to 2025. It highlights that WHO's one-dose recommendation in 2022 was most strongly associated with increased vaccine introductions, while Gavi's funding policy expansion (2017-2025) also played a role in some models. Changepoint analysis identified a significant increase in introductions in 2022, with model projections estimating 22.46 additional national introductions. The study provides actionable insights for improving equitable vaccine access, though it does not explicitly report limitations. The evidence is based on statistical modeling and changepoint analysis, which may introduce some uncertainty.

title: The Vaginal Microbiome Across the Continuum from HPV Infection to Cervical Cancer: A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection serves as the core prerequisite for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and invasive cervical cancer. This review explores the bidirectional regulatory crosstalk between vaginal microbiota and HR-HPV across the cervical cancer continuum, focusing on microbial dysbiosis, its impact on viral infection, and the progression to cervical cancer.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We conducted a narrative review of studies published primarily between January 2021 and April 2026. PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP were searched using terms related to the vaginal microbiome, HR-HPV infection, CIN, cervical cancer, underlying mechanisms, microbial biomarkers, and microbiome-modulating interventions. Relevant peer-reviewed epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical studies were prioritized, and the manuscript was prepared with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Dysbiosis disrupts vaginal acidic barriers, reshapes local cytokine networks, impairs antiviral innate immunity, and modulates HPV E6/E7 oncogenic transcription; reciprocally, HR-HPV oncoproteins remodel microbial community structures to sustain a dysbiotic feedback loop. Three core carcinogenic cascades induced by dysbiotic flora are elaborated: epithelial barrier erosion, metabolic reprogramming, and epigenetic rewiring of host and viral genomes. Dynamic microbial characteristics corresponding to all stages of progressive cervical lesions, from transient HPV infection to high-grade CIN and carcinoma, are sorted out.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Current bottlenecks, including inconsistent probiotic standards, preclinical model limitations, and unresolved gut–vagina microbiome interactions, require further investigation before widespread clinical translation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The bench-to-bedside translational progress of microbiome-targeted interventions is summarized, including single/multi-strain probiotic supplementation, engineered lactic acid bacterial therapeutic vaccines, vaginal microbiota transplantation, and traditional Chinese medicine therapy that reconstructs vaginal eubiosis. The clinical application of microbial diversity, strain-level single-nucleotide variants, and taxonomic biomarkers for early screening, efficacy prediction, and postoperative recurrence risk stratification is illustrated.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the bidirectional relationship between the vaginal microbiome and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) across the cervical cancer continuum. It highlights how microbial dysbiosis, characterized by depleted lactobacilli and overgrown anaerobic pathogens, creates a pro-inflammatory, immune-suppressive environment that promotes HR-HPV persistence and malignant transformation. The review outlines three core carcinogenic cascades: epithelial barrier erosion, metabolic reprogramming, and epigenetic rewiring. It also summarizes the translational progress of microbiome-targeted interventions, such as probiotics, therapeutic vaccines, and microbiota transplantation, and discusses their potential in early screening and risk stratification. Despite these insights, challenges like inconsistent probiotic standards, preclinical model limitations, and unresolved gut–vagina microbiome interactions remain, necessitating further research for clinical application.

title: Contemporary global prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus among female sex workers, 2015–2025: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Abstract Background Female sex workers experience disproportionate exposure to human papillomavirus (HPV), but estimates of HPV prevalence and genotype distribution vary according to geography, specimen type, diagnostic method, and genotype coverage.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This updated systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized contemporary evidence published between February 2015 and December 2025.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Results Thirty-six independent study/population estimates from 23 countries included 12,193 female sex workers, of whom 5,586 were HPV positive.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, subgroup patterns, and sensitivity analyses were examined.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The broad genotype distribution includes both vaccine-targeted and non-vaccine types and underscores the relevance of vaccination, cervical cancer screening, and integrated STI/HIV prevention services for this population.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes contemporary evidence on HPV prevalence among female sex workers globally, indicating a substantial burden with significant heterogeneity and genotype distribution.

title: Acceptability and preference of self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus DNA testing compared with physician-collected Pap smear.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Self-collected vaginal sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing provides a promising alternative to physician-collected Pap smears, especially in low-resource settings. However, data on its acceptability and preferences among Filipino women remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 592 women. Participants underwent both physician-collected Pap smears and self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing.
analysis.methods: Perceptions were measured using five-point Likert scale questionnaires before and after self-collection. Descriptive statistics were used, and paired and independent Wilcoxon tests were used to compare Likert responses. Willingness to undergo screening was analyzed with Cochran's Q and McNemar tests. Participants' reasons for their preferred screening method were categorized thematically and displayed in stacked bar charts.
analysis.main_results: Self-collection was generally viewed as painless, not uncomfortable, non-embarrassing, and easy and convenient. Acceptability significantly increased after participants performed self-collection (P < 0.001 for pain and discomfort). Compared with Pap smears, self-collection was seen as less embarrassing (P < 0.001), but rated as less easy (P = 0.01) and less convenient (P = 0.004). Most participants preferred physician-administered screening (84.8%) due to trust in medical expertise, and confidence in the procedure's accuracy, safety and cleanliness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Self-collected vaginal sampling was highly acceptable, yet physician-collected screening remained the preferred method. Improving education, demonstrations, and support for self-collection may enhance the uptake of HPV DNA testing and broaden access to cervical cancer screening in the Philippines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform strategies to improve the uptake of HPV DNA testing and broaden access to cervical cancer screening in the Philippines by highlighting the need for education and support for self-collection methods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate as it provides insights into acceptability and preferences but does not establish causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the acceptability and preferences of self-collected vaginal samples for HPV DNA testing compared with physician-collected Pap smears among 592 Filipino women. The research aimed to understand women's perceptions, experiences, willingness, and preferences regarding these screening methods. Using five-point Likert scale questionnaires and statistical tests, the study found that self-collection was generally viewed as painless, non-embarrassing, and convenient, with acceptability increasing after participants performed the task. However, most women preferred physician-administered screening due to trust in medical expertise and confidence in its accuracy, safety, and cleanliness. The study highlights the potential of self-collection to improve access to cervical cancer screening in low-resource settings, but emphasizes the need for education and support to enhance its uptake. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data.

title: Caregiver knowledge and Attitudes toward Human Papillomavirus Vaccination among adolescent girls living with HIV in Sierra Leone: A health facility-based cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate caregiver knowledge, willingness, and barriers to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination among adolescent girls living with HIV in Sierra Leone, addressing the gap in understanding how these factors influence vaccination decisions in this specific population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A health facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 249 caregivers of adolescent girls living with HIV in Sierra Leone, focusing on their awareness and attitudes toward HPV vaccination.
analysis.methods: Structured questionnaires were used to collect data at public tertiary hospitals and high-volume HIV clinics, with statistical analyses including chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kruskal-Wallis tests to assess associations.
analysis.main_results: Only 32.1% (80/249) of caregivers had heard of HPV, and fewer were aware of its link to cervical cancer (24.4%, 60/246) or prevention methods (31.9%, 79/248). Misconceptions were common, with 16.3% (36/221) linking oral contraceptives to cervical cancer, and 61.1% (44/72) of caregivers unwilling to vaccinate citing distrust in vaccine efficacy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reveals a significant knowledge-action gap, as tertiary-educated caregivers had the highest knowledge but similar willingness to vaccinate as less-educated groups, indicating that knowledge alone does not translate to action.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for culturally tailored education to address misconceptions and improve vaccination uptake, as well as the integration of HPV vaccination and cervical cancer screening into HIV care services.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Structural barriers, such as unawareness of the vaccine and missed vaccination days, were prominent, and the evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated caregiver knowledge, willingness, and barriers to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination among adolescent girls living with HIV in Sierra Leone. It found that only 32.1% of caregivers had heard of HPV, with even fewer aware of its link to cervical cancer or prevention methods. Misconceptions, such as linking oral contraceptives to cervical cancer, were prevalent, and distrust in vaccine efficacy was a major barrier. Tertiary-educated caregivers had the highest knowledge but similar willingness to vaccinate as less-educated groups, highlighting a knowledge-action gap. Structural barriers, including unawareness of the vaccine and missed vaccination days, were significant. The study suggests the need for culturally tailored education and integration of HPV vaccination into HIV care services. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias.

title: HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Persistent Oral High-Risk HPV Detection: A Narrative Review of Longitudinal Assessment, Diagnostic Evaluation, and Surveillance

analysis.scope_and_question: Currently, no validated population-based screening strategy uses persistent oral high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) detection to identify individuals at clinically meaningful risk of HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The literature published from January 2020 through June 2026 and identified in PubMed was synthesized by clinical context, specimen source, biological target, study population, and intended use.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Repeated detection of the same high-risk HPV genotype in serial oral specimens provides a pragmatic measure of persistent oral HPV detection but does not establish uninterrupted infection, sustained viral oncogene transcription, malignant transformation, or future OPSCC risk.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Oral HPV DNA, oral E6/E7 mRNA, tumor-tissue HPV testing, and plasma circulating tumor HPV DNA represent distinct biological and clinical signals.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clinical translation requires standardized longitudinal protocols, validation in intended-use populations, actionable management pathways, and incremental predictive value for proposed risk-stratification models.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review focuses on the role of persistent oral high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) detection in identifying individuals at risk for HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). The review synthesizes evidence from studies published between January 2020 and June 2026, sourced from PubMed, and categorizes findings by clinical context, specimen source, and intended use. It highlights that repeated detection of the same HPV genotype in oral specimens is a practical measure but does not confirm uninterrupted infection or future cancer risk. The review also notes that different HPV detection methods, such as oral HPV DNA, E6/E7 mRNA, tumor-tissue testing, and plasma circulating tumor HPV DNA, provide distinct biological and clinical signals. Finally, it emphasizes the need for standardized protocols, validation in target populations, and actionable pathways for clinical translation.

title: Phosphorylated HPV‐16 E7 disrupts planar cell polarity in cervical cancer cells through vangl1 dysregulation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the role of phosphorylated HPV-16 E7 in disrupting planar cell polarity (PCP) through Vangl1 dysregulation, addressing the need to delineate the consequences of E7 phosphorylation on HPV-driven transformation and malignant progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved CaSki cells and ectopic expression models to investigate the interaction between HPV-16 E7 and Vangl1, focusing on the effects of CKII-mediated phosphorylation on Vangl1 homeostasis and epithelial organization.
analysis.methods: Proteomics, biochemical, and cell-based assays were used to establish the interaction between CKII-phosphorylated HPV-16 E7 and Vangl1, and to assess the effects of E7 on Vangl1 homeostasis and epithelial structure.
analysis.main_results: The study found that CKII-mediated phosphorylation of HPV-16 E7 is required for Vangl1 recruitment, leading to a biphasic proteostatic imbalance where phosphorylated Vangl1 is aberrantly stabilized. E7 expression disrupts Vangl1 homeostasis, and Vangl1 siRNA-mediated ablation in CaSki spheroids mimics E6/E7 loss, leading to disrupted spheroidal architecture, reduced invasion, and increased sensitivity to chemotherapeutic stress.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified Vangl1 as a novel, phosphorylation-dependent interactor of HPV-16 E7, revealing a new mechanism by which HR HPVs might disrupt epithelial organization. This finding positions Vangl1 as a potential druggable target in HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting Vangl1 could be a therapeutic strategy for HPV-associated cervical cancer, as Vangl1's stabilization by E7 disrupts epithelial structure and promotes malignant traits.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single cell line and ectopic expression models, which may not fully represent the complexity of in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in vitro models.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified Vangl1 as a novel interactor of phosphorylated HPV-16 E7, revealing a new mechanism by which HR HPVs disrupt epithelial organization. The findings suggest Vangl1 as a potential druggable target for HPV-associated cervical cancer.

title: Real-world safety data of human papillomavirus vaccines after marketing in Shandong, China, August 2017–October 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the safety of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines after their introduction in China, addressing the growing need to ensure their safety as vaccination volumes increased.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A real-world safety study was conducted in Shandong, China, between August 2017 and October 2025, utilizing data from the Chinese National AEFI Information Management System (CNAEFIs) and the Shandong Provincial Immunization Program Information Systems (SDIPIs).
analysis.methods: A Univariate Poisson regression model was used to explore risk factors associated with HPV vaccine adverse events following immunization (AEFI), and disproportionality analysis was performed to detect abnormal signals.
analysis.main_results: From August 2017 to October 2025, 1056 AEFI cases were reported, with an overall rate of 7.99 per 100,000 doses. Of these, 1008 cases (95.46%) were mild vaccine-related reactions, and 15 cases (1.42%) were rare adverse reactions. Myalgia, induration with a diameter greater than 5 cm, immune thrombocytopenia, and mild reactions such as fatigue, drowsiness, dizziness, and headache were detected as abnormal signals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a low reporting rate of AEFI and a predominantly mild safety profile for the HPV vaccine, which is a novel observation in the context of real-world post-marketing data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies by reinforcing the safety of HPV vaccines and supporting continued vaccination programs to prevent HPV-associated diseases such as cervical cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on passive reporting systems, which may underrepresent rare adverse events, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the safety of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in Shandong, China, from August 2017 to October 2025. It highlights the importance of monitoring vaccine safety as usage increases, utilizing post-marketing data from national and provincial systems. The results show a low overall adverse event reporting rate, with most cases being mild. The authors interpret these findings as indicating a good safety profile for the HPV vaccine, which has implications for public health and vaccination programs. However, the study's reliance on passive reporting systems limits the confidence in its conclusions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Knowledge of Human Papillomavirus and Willingness to Recommend HPV Vaccination for Young Girls Among Doctors in Peshawar: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, which remains an important public health problem in low- and middle-income countries. HPV vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing HPV-related disease, but vaccine uptake in Pakistan remains limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026 among 189 registered doctors in public sector hospitals in Peshawar. Participants completed a structured, self-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of HPV infection and vaccination, and willingness to recommend the vaccine.
analysis.methods: Knowledge scores were categorised as good, moderate, or poor. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, tests of association, and multivariable binary logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: The mean knowledge score was 12.71 ± 3.01, and 121 participants (64.0%) had good knowledge. Overall, 144 participants (76.2%) reported willingness to recommend HPV vaccination. Doctors who had received formal HPV training had higher mean knowledge scores than those without prior training (13.97 ± 1.84 vs. 12.38 ± 3.17; p < 0.001). Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Higher HPV knowledge was associated with greater adjusted odds of willingness to recommend vaccination, although the overall multivariable model had limited explanatory power. Most doctors in Peshawar demonstrated good HPV-related knowledge and reported a high willingness to recommend HPV vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening HPV-related education, together with clear clinical and implementation guidance, may support physicians in communicating HPV vaccination to eligible adolescents as vaccination programmes expand in Pakistan.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The overall multivariable model had limited explanatory power, and the study was conducted in a single city, which may limit generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed HPV-related knowledge and willingness to recommend vaccination among doctors in Peshawar, Pakistan. The study found that most doctors had good knowledge of HPV and were willing to recommend vaccination, with higher knowledge associated with greater willingness. However, the multivariable model had limited explanatory power, and the study's findings may not be generalizable beyond Peshawar. The results suggest the importance of strengthening HPV education and providing clear guidance to support physicians in promoting vaccination as programs expand in Pakistan.

title: Factors influencing human papillomavirus school-based immunization in Alberta: a qualitative inquiry

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand barriers and enablers of human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization in Alberta, as vaccine coverage remains suboptimal despite the preventable nature of HPV infections and associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This qualitative inquiry involved virtual interviews with parents/guardians of school-aged children (11–17 years old) and virtual focus groups with program stakeholders, including leaders and front-line workers, across Alberta's health zones.
analysis.methods: The study used virtual interviews and focus groups, with data analysis guided by the Conceptual Framework of Access to Health Care and template thematic analysis.
analysis.main_results: Enablers of HPV immunization included convenience of the school-based program, normalization of the vaccine alongside other routine vaccines, relationship building with schools, parents/guardians, and communities, messaging that included personal stories, and youth engagement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the need to improve HPV messaging to address knowledge gaps and misconceptions, which is a novel insight for enhancing immunization programs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform strategies to improve HPV immunization programs by addressing knowledge gaps, enhancing communication, and fostering community engagement.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to qualitative data from virtual interviews and focus groups, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of quantitative measures and potential biases in self-reported data.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores barriers and enablers of human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization in Alberta's school-based program. The research aimed to address suboptimal vaccine coverage by understanding factors influencing uptake across health zones and population groups. Virtual interviews with parents/guardians and focus groups with program stakeholders were conducted, guided by the Conceptual Framework of Access to Health Care. Results identified enablers such as convenience, normalization with other vaccines, relationship building, and youth engagement, alongside barriers like knowledge gaps and immunization anxiety. The authors concluded that improving HPV messaging is crucial to address misconceptions. The study's findings can inform public health strategies to enhance immunization programs. However, the qualitative nature of the data and potential biases limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

title: HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS GENOTYPE DISTRIBUTION AMONG ADULT WOMEN IN THE RABAT REGION (MOROCCO): A RETROSPECTIVE AND ANALYTICAL STUDY WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR HPV VACCINATION STRATEGIES.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in Morocco, where it is the second most frequent cancer among women. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the primary etiological factor.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, descriptive, and analytical study was conducted at the Mohammed V Military Teaching Hospital, Rabat, Morocco, between May 2023 and April 2025. Asymptomatic women aged 30-65 years undergoing routine cervical cancer screening were included.
analysis.methods: Cervical samples were collected using liquid-based cytology medium and analyzed for HR-HPV using the Cobas® 4800 assay. Samples positive for pooled HR-HPV (excluding HPV16/18) underwent extended genotyping using the HPV002® assay. Sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical data were collected via standardized questionnaires. Statistical analysis included prevalence estimates, univariate, and multivariate logistic regression to identify factors independently associated with HR-HPV infection.
analysis.main_results: Of 2.235 eligible women, HR-HPV prevalence was 5.5% (n=123). HPV16 was the most prevalent genotype (19.5%), followed by HPV68 (12.2%), HPV31 (9.8%), HPV33 (7.3%), HPV35 (7.3%), and HPV39 (7.3%). Single-genotype infections predominated (95%), with dual infections in 5% of cases. Genotypes targeted by the 9-valent HPV vaccine accounted for 58.5% of infections. Multivariate analysis identified diabetes/immunosuppression, hormonal contraceptive use, and inflammatory cervical abnormalities as independent predictors of HR-HPV infection. 75% of HR-HPV-positive women were over 40 years, with a peak prevalence in the 50-59 age group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study provides the first detailed characterization of HR-HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in Moroccan women attending a tertiary hospital. HPV16 remains the predominant genotype.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the urgent need for expanded HPV vaccination and molecular-based screening programs in Morocco and provide a critical baseline for monitoring vaccine impact and guiding public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes among adult women in the Rabat region of Morocco, focusing on high-risk HPV types associated with cervical cancer. Conducted at the Mohammed V Military Teaching Hospital between May 2023 and April 2025, the retrospective analysis included asymptomatic women aged 30-65 undergoing routine cervical cancer screening. HPV genotypes were identified using the Cobas® 4800 assay, with extended genotyping for positive samples excluding HPV16/18. The study found that HPV16 was the most prevalent genotype, followed by HPV68, HPV31, HPV33, HPV35, and HPV39. Single-genotype infections were common, and genotypes targeted by the 9-valent vaccine accounted for 58.5% of infections. Multivariate analysis identified diabetes/immunosuppression, hormonal contraceptive use, and inflammatory cervical abnormalities as independent predictors of HR-HPV infection. The findings suggest the need for expanded HPV vaccination and screening programs in Morocco to address the prevalent genotypes and associated risk factors.

title: Beyond cervicovaginal limitations: potential bidirectional interactions between HPV infection and mucosal microbiota from oral, anorectal and penile sites — a mini-review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review explores the bidirectional interactions between human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and mucosal microbiota at oral, anorectal, and penile sites, with a focus on how these interactions may influence HPV persistence and malignant transformation. The central question is whether microbiota alterations contribute to HPV-related diseases beyond the cervicovaginal tract.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of sequencing and epidemiological evidence from studies on HPV and mucosal microbiota interactions. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods, but it summarizes findings from multiple sources on the topic.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that oral HPV infection alters microbial composition in a sex-, race-, and population-dependent manner. A tripartite oncogenic axis involving periodontal dysbiosis, high-risk HPV, and Candida albicans is implicated in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Additionally, periodontal inflammation independently increases susceptibility to oral HPV. In men who have sex with men, anorectal HPV-related lesions are associated with pro-inflammatory anaerobes like Bacteroides fragilis and Sneathia, and HIV or bacterial co-infections exacerbate mucosal dysbiosis. On penile skin, anaerobe-dominant community state types are linked to increased high-risk HPV risk, while HIV-induced dysbiosis may obscure HPV-specific microbial signatures.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited in its ability to fully characterize the microbiota signatures specific to HPV infection at penile sites due to the masking effect of HIV-induced dysbiosis. There is also a lack of comprehensive data on the role of microbiota in HPV-associated malignancies at non-cervicovaginal sites, particularly in diverse populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on elucidating the microbiota signatures specific to HPV infection in penile sites, accounting for HIV-induced dysbiosis. Additionally, there is a need for more studies on the role of microbiota in HPV-associated malignancies at non-cervicovaginal sites, with an emphasis on diverse populations. These findings could support the development of microbiota-based biomarkers and interventions for preventing non-cervical HPV-related cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This mini-review examines the bidirectional interactions between human papillomavirus (HPV) and mucosal microbiota at oral, anorectal, and penile sites, highlighting how these interactions may influence HPV persistence and malignant transformation. It identifies that oral HPV infection alters microbial composition in a sex-, race-, and population-dependent manner, with periodontal dysbiosis, high-risk HPV, and Candida albicans forming a tripartite oncogenic axis. In men who have sex with men, anorectal HPV-related lesions are associated with pro-inflammatory anaerobes, and HIV or bacterial co-infections worsen dysbiosis. On penile skin, anaerobe-dominant community state types increase high-risk HPV risk, while HIV-induced dysbiosis may obscure HPV-specific signatures. The review emphasizes the need for further research on microbiota-specific signatures and their role in non-cervical HPV-related malignancies, with implications for developing microbiota-based interventions.

title: In vitro and insilico antiviral activity of Polyscias scutellaria leaf extract against drug-susceptible and drug-resistant herpes simplex virus and human papillomavirus-positive cervical cancer: implications for topical formulation development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) and human papillomavirus (HPV) infections remain major global health concerns, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study examined the inhibitory effects of Polyscias scutellaria (Burm.f.) Fosberg, a tropical ornamental plant with edible young shoots and leaves against HSV, HPV, and cervical cancer cell growth.
analysis.methods: Four extracts prepared from fresh and dried leaves using ethanolic and hot-water methods were evaluated for their inhibitory activities against drug-susceptible and drug-resistant HSV and HPV, as well as for their effects on CaSki and HeLa cell growth, using plaque inhibition, HPV-16 pseudovirus binding, wound-healing, acridine/ethidium dual staining, and flow cytometry assays.
analysis.main_results: The ethanolic extract of fresh P. scutellaria exhibited the strongest inhibitory effects against both wild-type and drug-resistant HSV strains among all extracts tested and downregulated HSV-1 ICP4, UL30, US6 and gC. This extract also suppressed HPV-16 pseudovirus infection at an early stage. In addition, it reduced cancer cell proliferation and increased apoptosis, while suppressing HPV-16/18 E6, BCL2, and NFKB1 expression and upregulating BAX expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Gene and protein expression levels were analyzed by quantitative qPCR and western blot analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The putatively annotated metabolites with the highest peak area in P. scutellaria identified using electrospray ionization-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry, showed favorable drug-likeness and potential interactions with candidate HSV-1 and HPV-16 proteins by in silico analysis. A prototype herbal soap containing this extract significantly reduced drug-resistant HSV-1 infection and HPV-16/18 E6 expression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings highlight P. scutellaria as a promising natural antiviral and anticancer agent with potential for health-product development.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the antiviral activity of Polyscias scutellaria leaf extract against herpes simplex virus (HSV) and human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly in drug-resistant strains and HPV-associated cervical cancer. The research aimed to explore the potential of this plant extract as a topical formulation for antiviral and anticancer applications. The study evaluated four extracts using various assays, including plaque inhibition, HPV-16 pseudovirus binding, and flow cytometry, and found that the ethanolic extract of fresh leaves had the strongest inhibitory effects against HSV and suppressed HPV-16 pseudovirus infection. It also reduced cancer cell proliferation and increased apoptosis. The findings suggest that P. scutellaria could be a promising natural agent for developing health products targeting HSV and HPV infections. However, the study is limited to in vitro and in silico analyses, and further research is needed to validate these results in vivo.

title: Awareness and attitudes of health and non-health faculty students at the University of Split, Croatia about human papillomavirus vaccination: a cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge, perceptions, and behaviors of health and non-health faculty students in Croatia regarding human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, given the low vaccination rates in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2024, purposively approaching students at the University of Split enrolled in health-related and non-health-related programs.
analysis.methods: The study used a survey with 29 dichotomous (yes/no) and Likert-scale items in English. Chi-square tests were used to compare frequencies, and binomial logistic regression was applied in unadjusted and adjusted models to explore associations.
analysis.main_results: Two hundred and thirty-four (91.4%) health studies students compared to 178 (86.0%) non-health studies students were aware of the HPV vaccine. Less than one-third (n = 123/463, 27%) of the students self-reported being vaccinated against HPV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that non-health students had higher uncertainty about HPV as a cause of cancer and anogenital cancer, and that not wanting to seek more information was associated with not intending to get vaccinated.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health officials about the need for targeted interventions to improve HPV vaccination rates among students, particularly those who are knowledgeable but reluctant to seek more information.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, but the evidence is strong due to the use of statistical methods and the clear association of sociodemographic and behavioral factors with vaccination status.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed HPV awareness, perceptions, and vaccination behaviors among health and non-health students at the University of Split, Croatia. The survey, conducted from March to April 2024, included 29 items measuring knowledge, attitudes, and behavioral intentions. Results showed that 91.4% of health students and 86.0% of non-health students were aware of the HPV vaccine, while less than one-third (27%) reported being vaccinated. Non-health students exhibited higher uncertainty about HPV's role in cancer and were more likely to not intend vaccination if they lacked information. The study highlights the importance of addressing information gaps in HPV vaccination campaigns, particularly among non-health students. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, but the statistical methods used support the findings.

title: Wastewater-Based Surveillance of Human Papillomavirus Genotype Diversity

analysis.research_question_and_background: Objective To assess whether wastewater-based epidemiology can monitor the diversity and temporal circulation of HPV genotypes at the population level.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Design, Setting, and Participants This is a cross-sectional study of raw wastewater collected twice weekly from January 24, 2024, to January 29, 2025, at a large wastewater treatment plant serving approximately 1 million population equivalents in the Paris, France, metropolitan area.
analysis.methods: HPVs of the genus Alphapapillomavirus were quantified using a broad-spectrum quantitative polymerase chain reaction assay and normalized using human-associated excretion markers (crAssphage and mitochondrial DNA).
analysis.main_results: Results HPVs were detected in all 100 wastewater samples analyzed, with a mean concentration of 7.3 × 10 3 genome equivalents/L (range, 7.3 × 10 1 to 3.0 × 10 5 genome equivalents/L), showing moderate temporal variability over the study period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: High-risk HPV-39 and HPV-56, which are not covered by current vaccines, were detected in 72% (95% CI, 63%-81%) and 58% (95% CI, 48%-68%) of samples, respectively, vs 21% (95% CI, 13%-29%) for HPV-16 and 5% (95% CI, 1%-10%) for HPV-18, both of which are vaccine targeted.

analysis.summary_en: Objective To assess whether wastewater-based epidemiology can monitor the diversity and temporal circulation of HPV genotypes at the population level. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a cross-sectional study of raw wastewater collected twice weekly from January 24, 2024, to January 29, 2025, at a large wastewater treatment plant serving approximately 1 million population equivalents in the Paris, France, metropolitan area. HPVs of the genus Alphapapillomavirus were quantified using a broad-spectrum quantitative polymerase chain reaction assay and normalized using human-associated excretion markers (crAssphage and mitochondrial DNA). Results HPVs were detected in all 100 wastewater samples analyzed, with a mean concentration of 7.3 × 10 3 genome equivalents/L (range, 7.3 × 10 1 to 3.0 × 10 5 genome equivalents/L), showing moderate temporal variability over the study period. High-risk HPV-39 and HPV-56, which are not covered by current vaccines, were detected in 72% (95% CI, 63%-81%) and 58% (95% CI, 48%-68%) of samples, respectively, vs 21% (95% CI, 13%-29%) for HPV-16 and 5% (95% CI, 1%-10%) for HPV-18, both of which are vaccine targeted. Surveillance of circulating HPV genotypes at the population level remains limited because clinical monitoring primarily relies on cervical screening and does not capture infections in men or individuals outside screening programs. The most frequently detected genotypes were HPV-66 (97%; 95% CI, 93%-100%), HPV-6 (93%; 95% CI, 88%-97%), and HPV-53 (89%; 95% CI, 83%-95%).

title: Safety and Immunogenicity of First Russian Quadrivalent (Recombinant, Adsorbed) Human Papillomavirus (Types 6, 11, 16, 18) Vaccine in Children Aged 9–17 Years: Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Phase III Clinical Trial

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a significant risk factor for the development of HPV-associated precancerous and malignant diseases. The study aimed to address the need for evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of a Russian quadrivalent HPV vaccine in children aged 9–17 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, phase III clinical trial with a 1 : 1 participant allocation ratio was conducted. The study included healthy seronegative children aged 9–17 years. Participants aged 9–13 years received either the investigational vaccine or the reference vaccine.
analysis.methods: Vaccine safety was assessed from April 2, 2024, to April 14, 2025, in all participants who received at least one vaccine dose (as-treated population). The primary efficacy endpoint was the geometric mean titer ratio (GMT Ratio) of antibodies to HPV 1 month after full vaccination course (Per-Protocol (PP) population); additionally, the GMT Ratio was evaluated for every HPV type.
analysis.main_results: A total of 705 adverse events (AEs) were registered during the study period, 426 of which were considered related to vaccination. No severe vaccination-related AEs were reported. The investigational vaccine demonstrated comparable immunogenicity to the reference drug across all four HPV types in both age cohorts.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The investigational vaccine showed a favorable safety profile and adequate immunogenicity compared to the reference vaccine in children aged 9–17 years. The study provides evidence that the vaccine is immunogenic across all four HPV types in both age groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the investigational vaccine could be a viable option for preventing HPV-associated diseases in children. The comparable immunogenicity and favorable safety profile support its potential use in public health programs targeting HPV prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a specific population of healthy seronegative children, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is strong, with a high confidence assessment based on the randomized, double-blind design and the evaluation of both safety and immunogenicity endpoints.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a Russian quadrivalent HPV vaccine in children aged 9–17 years. The vaccine targets HPV types 6, 11, 16, and 18, and was compared to a reference vaccine. The trial was multicenter, randomized, and double-blind, with a 1:1 allocation ratio. A total of 705 adverse events were recorded, with 426 considered vaccine-related, but no severe events were reported. The investigational vaccine demonstrated comparable immunogenicity to the reference vaccine across all four HPV types in both age cohorts. The study found that the vaccine had a favorable safety profile and adequate immunogenicity in children. These results suggest the vaccine could be a promising tool for HPV-associated disease prevention in this age group. However, the study was limited to a specific population of healthy seronegative children, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, with a high confidence assessment due to the rigorous design and comprehensive evaluation of safety and immunogenicity.

title: A unique initiative: Human papillomavirus vaccination for girls in Assam, India

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of HPV vaccination programs in Assam, India, by initiating a unique initiative to vaccinate girls aged 9 years and above to prevent cervical cancer and raise awareness about HPV-related diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a vaccination initiative conducted in Assam, India, from March 2025 to February 2026, targeting girls aged 9 years and above. A total of 2000 girls received the vaccine, with 3800 doses administered.
analysis.methods: The initiative involved administering an indigenously made HPV vaccine, CERVAVAC, in collaboration with a nonprofit organization. The study focused on raising awareness and promoting vaccination among girls in the target population.
analysis.main_results: A survey revealed that less than 1% of girls in Assam had previously been vaccinated against HPV, and awareness was 39% among students of elite academic institutions due to factors such as lower socioeconomic status, population heterogeneity, and sociocultural beliefs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that sociocultural and economic factors significantly influenced HPV vaccination coverage and awareness, highlighting the need for targeted awareness campaigns in low-resource settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of addressing sociocultural barriers to improve HPV vaccination rates and cervical cancer prevention in regions with limited healthcare access.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single state and the use of survey data rather than clinical outcomes. However, the evidence is strong as it provides insights into the challenges of HPV vaccination in Assam, India.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the first HPV vaccination initiative in Assam, India, using the indigenously made vaccine CERVAVAC. The main objective was to increase vaccination rates and awareness among girls aged 9 years and above to prevent cervical cancer. A survey found that less than 1% of girls had previously been vaccinated, and awareness was 39% among students of elite institutions due to socioeconomic and cultural factors. The initiative highlighted the role of nongovernmental organizations in promoting vaccination and awareness. The study's findings emphasize the need for culturally sensitive strategies to improve HPV vaccination coverage in low-resource settings. However, the study is limited by its focus on a single state and reliance on survey data rather than clinical outcomes, which affects the strength of the evidence.

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection among women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China: a retrospective study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China, to provide insights into the epidemiological patterns of HPV in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, single-center study was conducted on 13,492 females aged 18–85 years who underwent HPV testing at the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou, China.
analysis.methods: Cervical cast-off cells were collected for HPV testing using low-density gene chip and flow hybridization technology. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to assess the relationship between HPV prevalence and age.
analysis.main_results: A total of 27 HPV types were detected, including 17 high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and 10 low-risk/uncertain oncogenic significance HPV (LR-HPV). The overall HPV infection rate was 16.86% (2,275/13,492), with 12.59% (1,699/13,492) being single HPV-type infections and 4.27% (576/13,492) being multiple HPV-type infections. The prevalence of HPV showed a "two-peak" age-related distribution, with peaks in the ≤29-year and ≥60-year age groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study revealed the basic genotype- and age-specific distribution of HPV infection among females in Zhangzhou, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and awareness of vaccination for the most prevalent HPV types.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide valuable insights for the measurement of HPV prevention interventions and emphasize the importance of regular HPV surveillance in this population, particularly for the highly prevalent HPV types.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single-center sample, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on direct HPV testing and statistical analysis of a large cohort.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection among 13,492 women aged 18–85 years undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China. The overall HPV infection rate was 16.86%, with HPV52 being the most prevalent type. The prevalence showed a "two-peak" age-related distribution, peaking in the ≤29-year and ≥60-year age groups. The study highlights the importance of targeted HPV surveillance and vaccination awareness for the most prevalent types. While the study is limited by its single-center design, the findings are robust and provide insights for HPV prevention interventions.

title: Parental perception and intention to vaccinate female children 9–14 years with the human papillomavirus vaccine in Ile-Ife, Nigeria: theory of planned behaviour approach

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess parental perceptions and intention to vaccinate female children against HPV in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, using the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). The scientific/public-health problem is the need to improve HPV vaccination coverage among eligible girls, as parental decision-making is crucial.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 163 parents of female children aged 9–14 years in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, using a multistage sampling technique.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a pretested questionnaire and analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27, with chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Of the 163 questionnaires distributed, 160 (98.2%) were completed. Higher education level and perceived behavioural control were associated with parental intention to vaccinate, with adjusted odds ratios of 6.06 and 11.97, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that both positive perception of HPV vaccination and parental intention to vaccinate were suboptimal, with perceived behavioural control and parental educational level being significant predictors of intention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that interventions aimed at strengthening parental intention to vaccinate should focus on these factors to improve HPV vaccination coverage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has a limited sample size and response rate, and the findings may not be generalizable to other populations. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed parental perceptions and intention to vaccinate female children against HPV in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, using the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Of 163 questionnaires, 160 were completed, with higher education level and perceived behavioural control significantly associated with intention to vaccinate.

title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Human Papillomavirus Prevention Health Literacy Scale for College Students in Taiwan.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus associated with several types of cancer. Because college students are a high-risk group, understanding their health literacy with regard to HPV prevention is critical.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional design was used, and the developed scale was validated on a sample of 372 college students from two universities in northern Taiwan and one university in central Taiwan.
analysis.methods: The initial scale comprised 49 items, developed from qualitative interviews and a literature review. After content validity assessment and item analysis, the scale was refined to 37 items. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted with 150 participants, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with 222 participants. Concurrent validity and internal consistency reliability were assessed.
analysis.main_results: The results of the EFA revealed a two-factor model accounted for 60.30% of the total variation, and those of the CFA demonstrated favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .02). Moreover, the average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, respectively, with corresponding composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating excellent convergent validity. Notably, the AVE surpassed the squared product-moment correlation of the corresponding factors, affirming good discriminant validity. The final iteration of the HPV-HLS comprised 21 items with two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information and seeking information from health care professionals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: After rigorous psychometric testing, the newly developed HPV-HLS demonstrated excellent reliability and validity, establishing it as an objective tool for evaluating HPV prevention health literacy among college students.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This HPV-HLS may be used by health care providers and educators to assess health literacy and evaluate the effectiveness of clinical interventions to prevent HPV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a psychometric tool, the HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS), for assessing HPV prevention health literacy among college students in Taiwan. The research was grounded in the context of HPV as a common sexually transmitted virus linked to various cancers, highlighting the importance of addressing health literacy in high-risk groups. A cross-sectional design was employed, involving 372 students from three universities in different regions of Taiwan. The scale was developed through qualitative interviews and literature review, then refined to 37 items following content validity and item analysis. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted with 150 and 222 participants, respectively, to evaluate the scale's structure. The final scale included 21 items divided into two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information, and seeking information from health care professionals. The results showed a two-factor model explaining 60.30% of the total variation, with favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, SRMR = .02). The average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, with composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating strong convergent validity. The AVE exceeded the squared product-moment correlation, confirming good discriminant validity. Concurrent validity was supported by a correlation of .68 with the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire (p < .001), and internal consistency was demonstrated with a Cronbach's α of .959. The authors concluded that the HPV-HLS is a reliable and valid tool for assessing HPV prevention health literacy, which can inform health care providers and educators in evaluating interventions to prevent HPV infection. The evidence is strong, with no reported limitations.

title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between the cervicovaginal microbiome and HPV infection, particularly focusing on how viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) might influence this relationship.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study analyzed 311 non-pregnant women to characterize cervicovaginal microbiome composition and functional potential across HPV infection status, viral type categories, cervical cytological grades, and CSTs.
analysis.methods: The study used whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing, integrated diversity analyses, MaAsLin2 differential abundance testing, and HUMAnN 3.0 functional pathway profiling to assess microbiome composition and functional potential.
analysis.main_results: HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial species richness and a reciprocal Lactobacillus-to-Gardnerella dominance shift compared to HPV-negative samples. HPV Other had the highest bacterial species richness and distinct taxonomic and predicted functional associations, including higher inferred abundance of siderophore- and lipopolysaccharide-biosynthesis pathways. CST IV showed pronounced Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was associated with lower Fannyhessea vaginae and Alloscardovia omnicolens abundance and higher Phocaeicola vulgatus abundance relative to NILM.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity are not aligned, and that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the microbiome's role in HPV infection and its potential implications for cervical disease progression, highlighting the importance of CST in modifying HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and the results are based on inferred functional pathways rather than direct measurements, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the cervicovaginal microbiome's relationship with HPV infection, focusing on viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST). Using metagenomic sequencing and functional pathway analysis, the research found that HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial diversity and a shift in Lactobacillus-to-Gardnerella dominance. HPV Other was associated with the highest species richness and distinct functional profiles, while CST IV exhibited significant Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was linked to reduced abundance of certain bacteria and increased Phocaeicola vulgatus. The authors suggest that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions, indicating that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity may not be directly aligned. These findings could inform future studies on microbiome-based interventions for HPV-related cervical disease. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the use of inferred functional pathways may affect the strength of the evidence.

title: Sexual Function and Psychological Distress Across Surveillance, Colposcopy, and LEEP in Women with a History of High-Risk HPV Positivity: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether the burden of sexual function and psychological distress differs across the successive steps of cervical management in women with a history of high-risk HPV positivity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center cross-sectional study was conducted involving 302 reproductive-age women with a history of hrHPV positivity, divided into three groups: surveillance (n = 50), colposcopy (n = 177), and loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) (n = 75).
analysis.methods: Participants completed the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), WHOQOL-BREF, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Groups were compared using Kruskal–Wallis and chi-square tests, while FSFI total was modelled by multivariable linear regression and FSFI-defined dysfunction by logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in FSFI total, subdomains, HADS, or WHOQOL domains. FSFI-defined dysfunction was frequent across groups, with no statistically significant difference (59–67%). Depressive symptoms were associated with FSFI-defined dysfunction (OR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.03–1.26, p = 0.009), but not with continuous FSFI (B = −0.37, p = 0.064). Marital status was the strongest overall correlate.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that sexual function did not differ significantly between management groups, and in exploratory analyses, depressive symptoms showed the most consistent association with sexual dysfunction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the importance of considering psychosocial and relational factors in the psychosexual care of women with a history of hrHPV positivity, highlighting the need for further research into screening and counseling strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and the adjusted models showed no significant association between management pathway and FSFI, suggesting the evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the impact of high-risk HPV management steps—surveillance, colposcopy, and LEEP—on sexual function and psychological distress in 302 reproductive-age women. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing sexual function, quality of life, and psychological well-being. No significant differences were observed in sexual function or psychological distress across the groups. Depressive symptoms were associated with sexual dysfunction, but this link was not significant in continuous FSFI models. Marital status emerged as the strongest correlate. The authors suggest that psychosocial factors may influence sexual health outcomes in women with a history of hrHPV positivity, though they caution that prospective studies are needed before making specific recommendations. The study's cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the evidence strength is moderate.

title: AI Chatbot Use for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Literacy in Japan

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the issue of persistent misinformation and low confidence in HPV vaccine uptake in Japan by evaluating the efficacy of an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot compared to a government leaflet.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A parallel-group randomized clinical trial was conducted among female caregivers in Japan with unvaccinated daughters aged 12 to 18 years, comparing the immediate and 2-week durability of HPV vaccine literacy between the chatbot and leaflet groups.
analysis.methods: HPV vaccine literacy was measured using 7 factual questions, and the primary outcome was assessed immediately after the intervention and at 2-week follow-up. The secondary outcome was the decision to vaccinate at 2 weeks.
analysis.main_results: The chatbot group showed higher HPV vaccine literacy immediately after the intervention and at 2-week follow-up compared to the leaflet group, with no measurable effect on vaccination decisions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concluded that an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot improved HPV vaccine literacy more than a government leaflet, with effects lasting up to 2 weeks, but did not significantly impact vaccination decisions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that conversational AI may complement official materials and health care professional recommendations in enhancing HPV vaccine literacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the limited sample size and the short follow-up period, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: A randomized clinical trial in Japan found that an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot improved immediate and 2-week HPV vaccine literacy among caregivers, without affecting vaccination decisions.
